sections.1. What it owns and what it may read:
- Owns: `research/**` on the bridge (this charter, `hypotheses/REGISTER.md`, one folder per experiment under
  `experiments/<id>/` with its preregistration, run records, results ledger and report), `reads/` (design reads to the visionary and fetch asks), `research.html` with its data record, `handoff/LANE-RESEARCH-LAB.md`,
  memory files named `research-<id>`. A repository of its own only when an experiment needs continuous integration
  and the verifier; then the monitor numbers it under the session map and the owner installs the verifier's entry.
- Reads, read-only: the roadmap record and the architecture snapshots; the published contracts of the platform
  repository through git-archive exports at a pinned commit; the conformance-labs simulation harness through an
  export at a pinned commit (never its oracle tests, never a worktree of another session); the programme's handoff
  and merge-decision records through the masking reader; the R&D report (`visionary/RD-REPORT.md`). Nothing from the
  operator repository beyond the published interface contracts.
- Never: product code, packets, roadmap writes, the verifier, lanes.json or other sessions' files; no network unless
  the owner approved the exact fetch; no cloud spend without an approved run plan.
sections.1a. The procedure (owner instruction, 20:
The lab works as a research team, per scope: observe the situation (roadmap, development, architecture, PRs: what is
going on and why the scope matters now); hypothesise (what can be done for better performance, accuracy, assurance or
cost); collect the data the hypothesis needs, from the platform's records, the repositories' exports and the
literature, each source by digest; design and test (the protocol below); report and prove. One progress document per
scope under `research/progress/` is the owner's reading view and is kept current at every result. For the question
"what others have done so far" the lab may use deep search (the session's web search and fetch tools; the owner's word
of 2026-11-06); every source read is recorded with its identifier and digest, every fetch is reported to the monitor,
and nothing from the programme's own records leaves the session in a query.
sections.2. The experiment protocol:
Every experiment has an id `RL-nn`, a hypothesis from the register, and these records in order:

1. Preregistration (`PREREG.md`), before any run: the hypothesis as a falsifiable statement; the inputs by sha256
   (exports, records, fixtures) and the commit each came from; the design (factors, seeds with k >= 3 where the
   run is stochastic, splits declared before the run); the bounds and the gate (the run-manifest contract's
   paired, task-clustered interval and non-inferiority rule where they apply); the compute plan (light on this host
   through the monitor's heavy queue, or a lab run plan for cloud capacity), with the stream (S1-S4) and, for product-coupled runs, the ECU count (one ECU = one pass over the four frozen banking use cases for one configuration tuple at k >= 3 seeds; a planning count, never a reported result); what counts as PASS, FAIL and
   UNRESOLVED; and its sha256 recorded in the register.
   1a. Independent review (`PREREG-REVIEW.md`), before any run, by a pass that holds only the PREREG, the register
   row and this charter, never the run script: checks R1 falsifiable and exhaustive criteria; R2 clause scope (the
   unit the hypothesis names is the unit the measurement counts); R3 every input by digest, present; R4 bounds with
   units, gate, seeds, splits; R5 compute plan with stream and ECU count; R6 privacy; R7 the dataset's generation is
   independent of the hypothesis or the dependence is declared. A FAIL returns the PREREG to a new version before it
   is frozen; both digests go to the register. Adopted 2026-11-05 (RD-D1 (c)); applies from RL-14.
2. Run records: one per run, with the environment digest, the seed, the wall time and host load, and the outputs by
   reference (content hashes), never copied into the record.
3. Results ledger (`RESULTS.json`): verdicts in the verdict-ledger form (PASS, FAIL or UNRESOLVED; evidence
   references; the bound, the measured value and the margin; unresolved checks named). The verdict is computed by the lab's evaluator script from the run records and the ledger names that script's digest; it is never written by hand in the pass that ran the experiment. A breach of a preregistered
   bound is a finding, never a reason to re-tune and re-run under the same id.
4. Report (`REPORT.md`): one page; what was asked, what was measured, what it means, what it does not show, and
   the proposal if any. Scanned for privacy before it leaves the folder.
5. Proposal (`PROPOSAL.md`, optional): a design read for the roadmap visionary through the lane monitor, naming
   the roadmap items it touches, the evidence state it would justify, and whether it is a roadmap shift. The
   visionary rules under the owner's delegation or routes it to the owner; the lab never writes the roadmap.

An experiment that would change what the product ships is a candidate for the harness-admission gate (MAS-RA-005:
offline evolution only, held-out tasks, an executor-model matrix, matched budgets); its artefact class in the
evolution-surface record names who may propose, test, approve and activate it. The owner promotes; the lab proposes.
sections.3. Rules the session keeps:
- One repository, one session: the lab shares no path with any other session and edits nothing outside
  `research/**` and its lane file.
- Compute: at most one heavy job, only on the monitor's GO, never while a verify runs or a dry run measures; the
  quiet-host rule for the platform's verifies binds the lab too. Heavy GOs follow the 60 / 25 / 15 split by queue class (Q qualification-critical, T topology, routing and memory, X the rest) over a rolling window of twenty GOs; the lab names the class in each GO request; light runs are outside the window. Larger runs follow the lab run-plan contract
  (machine type, region, duration, dated cost estimate, lease, teardown and residual check) and the owner's approval
  of the plan.
- Evidence: every number in a report traces to a run record and an input digest; figures from papers are marked as
  reported, not reproduced, unless the lab reproduced them. A result is reportable when it meets the six gates adopted from RS-2 (2026-11-05): a formal property checked against production vectors where one is claimed; a preregistered negative outcome still reported; an external baseline reproduced faithfully where one is used; a dataset generated independently of the hypothesis or the dependence declared; replication on a held-out split or a second verifier where the claim is about generalisation; an artefact another group could run.
- Privacy: `privacy_scan.py` over every file before it is reported; no e-mail addresses, name tokens, the owner
  handle, local paths, account names, key material or the legacy brand term in files, messages or memory.
- Independence: the lab's results are inputs to campaign records and roadmap notes, not gates; the conformance labs
  keep test strategy; the lab reads their harness, never their oracles.
- Owner delegation of 2026-10-22: the lab answers its own questions with the recommended option and stops for the
  owner on permissions (fetches, spend, a repository), critical choices (a hypothesis that needs product-level runs
  before the planes exist) and anything that could shift the roadmap.
- Usage: stop at a safe point when the account's 5-hour or weekly limit reaches 98 %.
sections.4. What the lab can do now and what wait:
Now, with no new infrastructure: the data studies on the programme's own records (the verify-time dataset, the
chain ablation from the compaction cost report, review independence, process mining of the handoff records,
adjudication rates) and simulation studies on an export of the conformance-labs deterministic harness (scaling and
claim collisions under leased and advisory claims). Waiting on the Alpha 2 path (plane bootstraps, the read-only
profile, the native Linux gate): the pairing matrix, the strategy experiment, the shadow-routing report and the cohort
evaluation on the banking scenarios. The register marks each hypothesis READY or BLOCKED with the item it waits on.
sections.5. Interfaces:
- Owner: opens the session, approves fetches, spend and repositories, promotes candidates.
- Lane-Monitor: the only owner interface for the lab; registration of `research/**`; the heavy queue; relays of
  proposals and answers; checkpoints (the monitor folds this folder into its checkpoints and never edits it).
- Roadmap-Visionary: receives proposals as design reads; records what the owner rules; keeps the register's roadmap
  references current at its locks.
- Build-R12-ConformanceLabs: the simulation harness is read at a pinned commit; a lab finding about a campaign goes
  to R12 through the monitor as an input, never as a change to its files.
sections.lead:
# Research-Lab: charter (drafted by the roadmap visionary, 2026-11-04; owner "Yes, draft them")

The session that runs the programme's research and development line in parallel with product development: it
holds the hypothesis register, runs preregistered experiments, judges their results in the verdict-ledger form,
reports them, and proposes what the results justify to the roadmap. It owns `research/**` on the bridge and no
repository. It writes no product code and no packets; what should enter the product goes through the roadmap
visionary as a proposal and through the harness-admission gate as a candidate. Everything it produces is evidence
and proposals, never authority.

report.asked:
**Asked.** Do review rounds and the independent oracle find different findings (H-09a)? Does the verifier refuse a
measurable fraction of PASS_FOR_PUSH heads (H-09b)? Are carried findings re-raised (H-09c)? Are later rounds'
findings new rather than repeats (H-09d, added in v2 from v1's descriptive result)?
report.context:
**What the findings show (descriptive, not gated).** Round 1 raises the MAJOR findings (16 of 19; 3 more in round 2;
none later); rounds 3 and later raise MINOR and NOTE findings only. MAJOR findings always block, MINOR block in 0.90,
NOTE never. Among dispositioned findings, MAJOR are ADDRESSED least often (0.68 of 19), MINOR 0.82, NOTE 0.81; the
median disposition comes one round after the raise. 91 findings carry no disposition (raised in a final round or
never dispositioned).
report.means:
**What it means.** Later rounds are not empty (v1) and their findings are of lower severity (v2): the review
chain's second and later rounds mostly refine. Whether a later round repeats an earlier finding under a new id is
exactly what the record cannot say, because the id scheme is per round. The oracle's independence (H-09's main
claim) is unmeasured.
report.measured:
**Measured.** v1 (REPORT.v1.md, RESULTS.v1.json 2a6648f3): 104 review rounds over 25 Build-R00 series at count
level. v2 adds J2 (sha256 d7e4ff31): 397 findings of the same series with kind, severity, blocking flag, a lane
finding id, the round that raised it and its latest disposition; no oracle verdicts exist in any record the monitor
can export. Both runs are light, deterministic and recorded (runs/run-001.md, runs/run-002.md).
report.proposal:
**Proposal.** RL-02-PROPOSAL, a design read for the visionary through the monitor, small and not a roadmap shift:
(1) give review findings a cross-round identity in the review-record form (a stable id, or a "supersedes" field
naming the earlier id) so re-raises and carried findings become measurable; (2) record the oracle's per-packet
verdict and test count in the merge-decision record (its `oracle` block exists in a few records) so H-09a can be
run. Until then H-09a, H-09c and H-09d stay UNRESOLVED-by-input.
report.verdict:
**Verdict: UNRESOLVED** (RESULTS.json, superseding v1 by digest).
- H-09a: not measurable; the oracle's verdicts are not recorded anywhere the lab can read. UNRESOLVED-by-input.
- H-09b: 1 of 9 matched PASS_FOR_PUSH heads refused (0.11, Wilson 0.02 to 0.44), below the 40-head bound.
- H-09c and H-09d: the preregistered identity (packet, series, finding id) cannot span rounds, because every one
  of the 381 lane-token ids ends its middle segment with the digits of the round that raised it (381 of 381; the 69
  repeated identities are same-round full-form pairs). H-09d's gate was met with 227 of 227 "new" findings and
  H-09c's re-raise fraction is 0 of 57, and both numbers are vacuous. The lab records the gate result and sets the
  claim verdicts UNRESOLVED with the validity check named, rather than report a PASS the design cannot support.

**Proposal.** RL-04-PROPOSAL, a design read for the visionary through the monitor, not a roadmap shift: a dated
note on MAS-STRATEGY-001 (and for Build-R12's campaign record) that leased exclusivity is a decentralized-topology

peer-to-peer and may omit them under a single coordinator, where they add about 30 percent to the makespan for no

report.verdict:
**Verdict.** H-13b **PASS by the preregistered gate** (median paired difference non-negative at every N ≥ 2 point;
pooled interval above zero), with the family split as the finding that matters: the whole effect is the
decentralized topology's, where advisory claims duplicate 23 to 63 percent of work and overlap claims in every

that account; the two runnable claims are supported.

report.asked:
**Asked.** Is the merge predicate a conjunction of independently produced records, and does it hold for every
merged packet (H-03)?
report.limits:
**What it does not show.** Nothing about whether the records are independent in fact (only that they are distinct
fields from distinct producers); nothing about the five earliest decisions (2026-10-20/21), which record a clean
merge state without a merge commit and fall outside the unit (descriptively 3 FAIL, 2 UNEVALUATED, for the same
reasons as above); nothing about the approval files' bytes, which the lab cannot read.
report.means:
**What it means.** The conjunction is real: four independent producers (reviewers, the verifier, the owner as
approver, the monitor as decider) each leave a record, and the head-bound booleans are never false. But the
predicate is not stationary: its conjuncts entered the record one at a time through October, so "holds for every
merged packet" is false over the whole history and true over the history since the record form stabilised. The
right formal statement is a time-indexed predicate P_t whose conjunct set is the record form in force at t.
report.measured:
**Measured.** The predicate was written before the run (PREREG v1 462f9cc1) as P = R ∧ V ∧ A ∧ I ∧ H ∧ T: review
evidence present; the verifier's conclusion success with a check-run reference; an approver; a decider distinct from
the approver; every head-bound boolean true; a transport approval for hosted repositories. It was evaluated by an
allowlist script over the 53 merge-decision records on the bridge (set digest b3370227), on the 47 records that name
a merge commit. Run 001 had a script defect (two bare-named bridge records classed as hosted); run 002 is the run of
record and the defect is disclosed in the ledger.

|---|---|---|---|
| R review evidence | 45 | 0 | 2 |
| V verifier success with check run | 43 | 4 | 0 |
| A approver present | 47 | 0 | 0 |
| I decider differs from approver | 47 | 0 | 0 |

report.proposal:

the merge-decision schema is next amended, state the merge predicate as P_t in the schema's README with the date
each conjunct became mandatory, and add `reviews` to the required set so R cannot be MISSING. The lab sends it
through the monitor after RL-02 v2 reports.

report.asked:
**Asked.** Do the roadmap build's validators refuse every seeded inconsistency class of the register (dangling
dependency; status against evidence state; score drift; a status change without an update entry; a stale snapshot
digest) and the lab's added class (a stale reference), naming the seeded edit, and refuse none of three benign
control edits? Preregistered as v5 (1e8dfc4a) after four failed reviews and one instrument stop (v1 56b2829f, v2
532b08a3, v3 cda3e838, v4 cf9fe7a9; `PREREG-REVIEW.md`). Everything ran on a pristine copy of `roadmap/` at bridge
commit fce8245b in the lab scratch; the bridge's `roadmap/` was never touched.
report.limits:
**What it does not show.** Nothing about validators the lab did not seed; three edits per class; one record; the
validators and the record share an author, so the four covered classes may reflect that author's own habits. The
digest class was seeded on research-source digests, the only digest-bearing fields of the record; the architecture
snapshots live in another file the build reads but the lab did not mutate.
report.means:
**What it means.** The build checks what it can see in one file: ids, dependency closure, status against evidence
state, factor ranges and keys, harness and codebase references, duplicate ids. It does not check that a status
change is accompanied by a dated update entry (the diff against the last snapshot records the change; it never
refuses it), and it does not check the research section's digests against anything, neither their length nor the
copied paper files. Two of M4's refusals show a different, useful rule firing: closing an item exposes dependents
whose BLOCKED status is stale. The attribution rule was strict by design: two refusals that did catch the seeded edit
("factor keys", "unknown codebase reference") are counted as unattributed because their words name neither the field
nor the seeded value; the descriptive count without that rule is 14 of 18.
report.measured:
**Measured.** 22 builds in 7.7 s (run-001 87f4ad62; data ed7ce16d; RESULTS 050c553c). The unmodified copy builds clean (exit
0, 0.81 s). Of the 18 seeded edits, 14 were refused by the build and 10 of those refusals carried a token specific to
the seeded edit; 0 of 3 controls were refused or crashed; no build crashed. Precision 10 of 14 refusals (0.714). Per
class, attributed / refused / seeded: M1 dangling dependency 3 / 3 / 3 ("unknown dependency"); M2 status against
evidence 3 / 3 / 3 ("is DONE but its evidenceState is PLANNED"); M3 score drift 2 / 3 / 3 (the out-of-range factors
by "rating B2 out of range"; the removed factor refused as "factor keys", a refusal that names neither `benefit` nor
`B2`, so unattributed by the preregistered rule); M4 status change without an update entry 0 / 2 / 3 (two edits
refused for a different reason, "X is BLOCKED with nothing blocking it": closing the item unblocked a dependent whose
status the record still said BLOCKED; the third built clean; no refusal mentions an update entry); M5 stale
reference 2 / 3 / 3 (the unknown codebase refused as "unknown codebase reference", unattributed by the token rule);
M6 stale snapshot digest 0 / 0 / 3 (a 63-character source digest, a replaced seed-paper digest with the file
unchanged on disk, and a replaced secondary-paper digest all built clean).
report.proposal:
**Proposal.** RL-15-PROPOSAL, a design read for the visionary through the monitor, not a roadmap shift: two
candidate validators for build_roadmap, each a data check of the kind it already runs, (1) refuse a status change
against the last snapshot that no update entry dated on or after the snapshot names (M4), and (2) refuse a
research-section digest that is not 64 hexadecimal characters, and, where a file under `research/papers/` is named,
one that does not match that file (M6); plus the observation that closing an item should also be refused while a
dependent still says BLOCKED, which the build already does. Whether these enter the builder is the visionary's call
under the owner's delegation; the lab writes no roadmap.
report.verdict:
**Verdict: FAIL as preregistered.** Two classes have 0 of 3 attributed refusals, M4 and M6, which is the FAIL
region; the PREREG named FAIL through M4 as the expected class and said an all-18 PASS was unreachable because M6's
third instance can be caught by no file comparison. FAIL here is the ordinary outcome of a benchmark, not a
near-miss of PASS: the validators cover the shape rules (M1, M2, M3, M5) and do not cover the process rule (M4) or
the digest rule (M6).

report.asked:
**Asked.** On the conformance labs' simulation harness at b4bbea79: are runs deterministic (H-27a); does the
committed REPLAY_STALE class row reproduce (H-27b); are duplicated and stale (reordered) board operations refused
after a run (H-27c); and does the recorded operation sequence, replayed through a fresh board, reproduce the claim
and merge answers, the register's own clause (H-27d)? Preregistered as v2 (77015690) after one failed review (v1
15939132; `PREREG-REVIEW.md`). The fault-class half of H-27 is a later id (BLOCKED on DATA-CORRECTNESS-001).
report.limits:
**What it does not show.** "The coordinator" is represented by `Board.apply` (the harness's coordinator board);
"reordered" is the stale-version late arrival, not a permuted log: both are proxies, declared. The stale vector was
posed at the deadline tick, after leases had expired, so the holder check fired first; a vector posed mid-run
(before expiry) would reach the version check and is a new id. Nothing about the production coordinator (R04/R08),
only the labs' simulation of the contracts.
report.means:
**What it means.** The exported harness is deterministic and its committed replay class reproduces; its board
refuses every duplicate before any other check and refuses every late versioned operation, though by holder and
merge state rather than by version at the deadline tick. The register's clause fails for a reason the design
predicts: the board reads the workers, the coordinator, the artefacts and the task-pass state for verification and
merge, so the effect log alone cannot replay merges through it. Replay safety in this harness rests on durable
simulation state, not on the log, which is the D1 question (RS-1 and RS-3: "replay safety often depends on durable
tool-side state"). The claim operations that need no such state (RELEASE, most ACQUIRE and RENEW) replay; VERIFY
and MERGE do not.
report.measured:
**Measured.** Run-001 35f3d6a9; data f5fe694a; RESULTS 7f8a3356. 13 classes x 32 seeds. H-27a: 416 of 416 run pairs
byte-identical. H-27b: C3's class row equal to the committed one (result PASS, no differing key). H-27c: 70,169
duplicate replays, all answered DUPLICATE_ID, none changed state; 39,795 stale replays (versioned operations with a
fresh id and the original expectedVersion, posed at the deadline tick), none accepted, none changed state, but none
answered STALE_VERSION: 30,504 were refused as NOT_HOLDER and 9,291 as MERGED. H-27d: 0 of 416 runs replayed the
claim and merge sequence identically through a fresh board; the first divergence was at a MESSAGE in 384 runs and at
a VERIFY in 32; every VERIFY replay (10,082) raised inside the board; agreement by kind: RELEASE 109 of 113, ACQUIRE
6,149 of 8,095, RENEW 17,686 of 25,223, ASSIGN 2,045 of 3,349, MERGE 817 of 9,461, MESSAGE 32 of 20,388, VERIFY 0.
report.proposal:
**Proposal.** None as a roadmap read. Two inputs: for R12 through the monitor, the stale-version vector mid-run
(a new id, RL-17 names it) and the observation that the board's refusal order is holder, state, then version; for
the visionary's DATA-CORRECTNESS-001 and D1 notes, that log replay through the board needs the durable state the
board consults, so the replay contract should name that state as an input, not only the event log.
report.verdict:
**Verdict: FAIL as preregistered, with one claim UNRESOLVED.** H-27a PASS; H-27b PASS; H-27c UNRESOLVED by the
preregistered rule (every stale replay was refused, but by the holder and state checks that run before the version
check, so the version rule itself was not shown; the lab expected STALE_VERSION and says so); H-27d FAIL, the
outcome class the PREREG named: the board is not a pure function of its operation stream. An exception in the
fresh-board replay counted as a divergence (review 2 note 3), and FAIL took precedence.

report.asked:
**Asked.** Can the arms study of CONF-MAS-003 (three arm policies against the defended baseline over five classes and
32 seeds) be expressed as MAS-RA-002's split declaration, run manifests, evaluation records and distribution-gate
comparisons that validate against the contract's schemas (H-31b), and do the gate's non-inferiority verdicts agree
with the campaign's recorded bound verdicts per arm and metric (H-31c)? First, as an instrument check, does the lab's
own validator and integer gate reproduce the contract's 85 vectors (H-31a)? Preregistered as v2 (eca606be) after one
failed review on scope (v1 7807d764; `PREREG-REVIEW.md`). Scope: the arms study only; the other four campaigns'
class rows are absolute bound checks with no baseline to pair against and are out of scope (PREREG section 0).
report.limits:
**What it does not show.** Nothing about the four other campaigns (out of scope by form); nothing about a real
model's manifests; the tolerance (10,000 ppm) and the agreement mapping are the lab's; five task clusters make the
gate's interval wide. The contract's semantic checks beyond the schema (the 17 refusal codes of the reference model)
were not run: the reference model script is not in the architecture export.
report.means:
**What it means.** The lab's reading of the contract is right: its gate reproduces every published vector bit for
bit, which is what the README promises any consumer. The arms study cannot be expressed as-is because the manifest
form requires a positive token budget per task: the contract assumes a model with tokens, and a deterministic
simulation has none. That is a finding about the record's form, not the lab's builder: the builder's other fields all
validate (the split, the comparisons, and the manifests and records on every other path). A sentinel budget (1 token)
or a declared "no model" configuration would express the study; either is a new id or a contract note. On agreement,
the two forms differ exactly where review 2's third note said they would: the campaign's verdict is a conjunction of
absolute per-class bound checks, the gate's is one pooled relative interval over five task clusters; a bound broken
in one class (A1 on C2) or two (A3 on C5 and C7) is averaged away by the pooled gate, which still finds the arm
non-inferior. A disagreement is a difference of forms, never an error in either record. Per-cell agreement is
reported above regardless of the verdict (note 1).
report.measured:
**Measured.** Run-001 b9efff33; data bb3b5cc8; RESULTS 6756016b. H-31a: 18 of 18 SHAPE vectors refused, 25 of 25 valid vectors
accepted, 17 of 17 valid comparison vectors reproduced bit for bit (decision, nonInferior, statistics) and both
DECISION_MISMATCH vectors flagged. H-31b: the split declaration validates and all 9 comparisons validate, but 0 of 640
manifests and 0 of 12 evaluation records do: every one is refused at `configuration.budget.tokensPerTask` against the
schema's minimum ({"tokensPerTask": {"minimum": 1, "maximum": 9007199254740991}, "costMicrosPerTask": {"minimum": 0, "maximum": 9007199254740991}, "wallClockSecondsPerTask": {"minimum": 1, "maximum": 9007199254740991}}); the lab's mapping gave the simulation a token budget of 0 because the harness
has no model and no tokens. H-31c: 7 of 9 cells agree. The two disagreements are both on duplicated work: A1 is
non-inferior to the baseline in the pooled gate (mean +3,880 ppm, half width 9,104) while the campaign records its
bound broken in class C2 alone; A3 is non-inferior (mean +3,982, half width 12,676) while the campaign records its
bound broken in C5 and C7. A2's duplicated work is not non-inferior in the gate (mean -16,275, half width 21,204) and
breaks the campaign's bound in every class: agreement. Completion and lost work agree in every cell (no difference
at all; mean 0, half width 0).
report.proposal:
**Proposal.** RL-18-PROPOSAL, a design read for the visionary through the monitor, not a roadmap shift: (1) for
MAS-RA-002's consumers, note that the manifest form cannot carry a configuration without a token budget; a
`tokensPerTask` of 0 with a stated reason, or an explicit "no model" configuration, would let simulation campaigns
use the record; (2) for CONF-A3-001 and MAS-RA-005, note that a pooled task-clustered gate and per-task absolute
bounds answer different questions, and a campaign that keeps per-class bounds should keep them beside the gate, not
replace them with it; (3) the register's H-31 is narrowed to the arms study, with the other four campaigns'
bound-check form named as what a second record would need.
report.verdict:
**Verdict: FAIL as preregistered on H-31b; H-31a PASS; H-31c UNRESOLVED (7 of 9, the inconclusive band).** The
monitor's GO is the recorded start word (review 2 note 2).

report.asked:
**Asked.** Are the figures the three owner-supplied syntheses (RS-1, RS-2, RS-3) attribute to the five papers the
owner approved for fetching found in those papers' own text, at a rate of at least 90 percent? Preregistered as v1
(317c3088), reviewed once (PASS; `PREREG-REVIEW.md`). 29 claims fixed before any search (`data/claims.json`).
report.limits:
**What it does not show.** Nothing about the figures the syntheses attribute to papers the lab does not hold (the
second-tier list, MAS-ProVe, VeriHarness and the rest); nothing about the syntheses' interpretations, only their
numbers; the hand pass is the lab's reading of first pages, not of every paper in full.
report.means:
**What it means.** The three syntheses report the five papers' figures faithfully with one exception, which all
three share (RS-2 and RS-3 cite RS-1 as a source, so one misreading travelled). The mechanical rate (82.8 percent)
is bounded by the lab's extractor, not by the syntheses: a space-aware extraction would have found four of the five
misses. The grounding method of the crosswalk (claim, pattern, context, verification by read) works on this corpus
with a stdlib extractor plus first-page reads; a full repeat needs either a better extractor or page reads for every
specific claim.
report.measured:
**Measured.** Run-001 6163a225; data 0a881349; RESULTS a211b180. The extractor found 24 of 29 claims (0.828): by paper,
Agentproof 6 of 6, Harness-Bench 3 of 5, the repeated-running paper 4 of 5, the Nature Machine Intelligence article
6 of 6, the memory-poisoning paper 5 of 7; by synthesis, RS-3 24 of 29, RS-2 9 of 11, RS-1 0 of 1. The five not found:
"more than 5,000 trajectories" (Harness-Bench), "ten backends" (Harness-Bench), "16 models" (repeated running),
"four memory write channels" and "nine structural vulnerabilities" (memory poisoning).
report.other:
**Hand pass, descriptive (review 1 note 1).** Of the 24 FOUND claims, 22 have a specific pattern (a decimal, a
percentage, a comma number or a name) whose context shows the synthesis's meaning: VERIFIED. Two short patterns
matched by coincidence first ("15" on an author line; "5,000" with an empty context) but are VERIFIED by the
first-page read of 2026-11-05 (the abstract states 15 temporal policies and graphs up to 5,000 nodes). Of the five
NOT_FOUND, four are the extractor's loss of word spacing in three PDFs, and the first-page reads of 2026-11-05 show
each figure as the syntheses state it: seven harnesses with ten backends; 16 models on 99 problems with two prompts
and five runs; four memory write channels and nine structural vulnerabilities. One claim is NOT VERIFIED: "more than
5,000 trajectories" for Harness-Bench (RS-1, RS-2 and RS-3 all state it); the paper's abstract gives 300 tasks, seven
harnesses and ten backends, and its text names 6,864 sampled runs; no figure of 5,000 appears. The syntheses' figure
may paraphrase the total runs; it is not in the text as stated. By hand: 28 of 29 claims verified, 1 not.
report.proposal:
**Proposal.** None as a roadmap read. For the crosswalk (F1): when the five papers enter it as OWNER_SUPPLIED
secondary papers, their figures can be marked verified at the claim level from this record, except Harness-Bench's
"more than 5,000 trajectories", which should be carried as "as reported by the syntheses, not found in the text". A
space-aware extractor is a new id if the lab repeats the step on more papers.
report.verdict:
**Verdict: UNRESOLVED as preregistered** (82.8 percent, between the 70 percent FAIL line and the 90 percent PASS
line).

report.asked:
**Asked.** Does a static checker written from MAS-RA-004's README reproduce the record's 52 topology vectors (H-25a),
and does the record refuse, with its own code and a witness, the three register classes the TopologySpec form can
express (cycle, unreachable node, budget escape), seeded once each on the 8 valid vectors, while accepting the valid
vectors (H-25b)? Preregistered as v1 (4f12f24f), reviewed once (PASS). The verdict is for H-25's TopologySpec half
and three of its five classes; the other two ("two writers", "unapproved effect path") the form cannot express.
report.limits:
**What it does not show.** Nothing about the WorkPlan and strategy halves; the edits and the checker share an
author; one edit per class per vector; "witness" is the refusing rule's named object, not a trace.
report.means:
**What it means.** The TopologySpec form, as published, already refuses the expressible classes by construction:
cycles are bounded by the depth-1 rule (a DELEGATE back-edge is MODE_STRUCTURE in every mode; MESSAGE cycles among
peers are allowed by design), unreachable nodes are refused in CENTRAL (the coordinator must delegate to every node)
and SINGLE_AGENT (no second node), and budget escapes are BUDGET. Two things the form does not do, for
GRAPH-COMPILE-001: it allows an isolated peer on a decentralized board (no reachability rule for peers), and it
carries no per-item writer and no effect marker, so "two writers" and "unapproved effect path" cannot be checked on
a TopologySpec; they need the WorkPlan and strategy records (BLOCKED) or the authority map. The lab's checker is a
second implementation of the record's rules that reproduces every vector, which is what MAS-RA-004's README promises
of any consumer (H-23's clean-room question, in part).
report.measured:
**Measured.** Run-001 37bd0922; data c6ee93f7; RESULTS e4c282b7. H-25a: the lab's checker agrees with all 52 topology vectors
(8 accepted, 44 refused with the expected code), including the baseline-record checks of MAS-RA-002 the selection
rule needs. H-25b: 21 of 22 gated edits refused with the expected code and a witness; all 8 valid vectors accepted;
the two decentralized "unreachable" edits (not gated) were accepted, as the record has no reachability rule for
peers. One gated edit was accepted: the budget edit on the one-node SINGLE_AGENT vector, where the construction
(agentBudget = max(1, nodes - 1)) yields 1, equal to the node count, so no escape was seeded.
report.proposal:
**Proposal.** None as a roadmap read. Input for GRAPH-COMPILE-001's design note (through the monitor): the three
expressible classes are covered by MAS-RA-004 as it stands; the checker's new work is the WorkPlan and strategy
layers (writers, effects, budgets across plans) and, if wanted, a reachability rule for decentralized peers.
report.verdict:

report.asked:
**Asked.** In harness-onion's published authority records at c1b838be: is every path under `architecture/` created by
exactly one packet authority (H-26a), and does every later change to such a path name its creator among the changer's
own baseline packets (H-26b)? Descriptively, how is ownership by the meta authorities laid out (H-26c)? Preregistered
as v2 (9eb03897) after v1 passed review but its chain rule proved uncomputable from the export; the overall verdict
rests on H-26b, since H-26a's count was seen in the inventory (review 2 note 1). Scope: the contract-text half under
this operationalisation, not the register's whole clause (revocation is RL-07's pinned-byte refusals; the board
traces wait on MAS-RA-009).
report.limits:
**What it does not show.** Nothing about revocation (RL-07 covers pinned bytes); nothing about runtime writers (the
board traces); nothing about files outside `architecture/`; the chain between meta generations needs git history.
report.means:
**What it means.** The published records already carry a writer-of-state discipline for the contracts: creation is
unique and every change is explicitly based, with the identity rule refusing edits to pinned bytes (RL-07). What the
records do not carry is a per-state single writer across time or the authority map the register names; those are
AUTHORITY-MAP-001's design and MAS-RA-009's board. The 12,080 out-of-scope changes show the same records govern
files beyond `architecture/`; a full-repository export would extend the census.
report.measured:
**Measured.** Run-001 62a328dd; RESULTS 82450439. 114 authority records: 92 packet authorities, 22 meta authorities. H-26a:
1,547 paths created, none created twice. H-26b: of 16,415 changed-file entries, 4,335 change paths created inside the
export and every one of them (4,335) names the creating packet among the changer's direct baseline packets; 12,080
entries change paths outside `architecture/` (docs, scripts, tests), which the export does not hold, and are not
gated. H-26c (descriptive): the meta authorities own 275 distinct paths, 139 of them in more than one generation;
`metaBaseline` is a commit id, so the generation chain is git history outside this export.
report.proposal:
**Proposal.** None as a roadmap read. For AUTHORITY-MAP-001's design (through the monitor): the packet authorities'
`newFiles` and `baselinePackets` already form a creator-and-basis graph over 1,547 published paths with no
duplicate creator; the map can be derived from them rather than written by hand, and the single-writer-across-time
question is the one it would add.
report.verdict:
**Verdict: PASS** (H-26a PASS; H-26b PASS, 4,335 of 4,335 linked), for the contract-text half under the
creator-linkage operationalisation: one creator per published path, and every published change explicitly built on
the creator. It is not "exactly one writer" in the register's sense: a path may be changed by many later packets,
each naming the creator, which is the chain's discipline (a change names what it builds on), not a single writer.

report.asked:
**Asked.** How far does MAS-RA-004's README section A2 alone carry another runtime: does a board state machine
written from it, with VERIFY's ledger rules declared un-modelled, reproduce the record's 32 transcript and 11 binding
vectors at a rate of at least 95 percent? Preregistered as v1 (511c8b66), reviewed once (PASS). Scope: the
coordinator half of H-23; the TopologySpec half is RL-20's (52 of 52); the strategy envelope has no record yet.
report.limits:
**What it does not show.** Nothing about the strategy envelope; the VERIFY binding and history rules were not
re-implemented; one implementation by one reader; the lab knew the vector categories and counts before writing.
report.means:
**What it means.** The README carries the coordinator contract to another runtime up to two points to ask its
author: the scope of `concurrency` (A2's wording against A1's definition) and the dependence of the binding and
VERIFY checks on MAS-RA-002's and MAS-RA-001's models, which a runtime must also implement or import. Everything
else in A2 (the operation table, expiry, the arbitration order, retries, the deadline, the transcript codes) replayed
as written, including the reversed-order vector. With the concurrency reading corrected the lab's machine would
reproduce 42 of 43, which would be a PASS; that is a new id, not a re-tune, and the report says so.
report.measured:
**Measured.** Run-001 9c0c21bf; data 1113270e; RESULTS 16915493. 38 of 43 vectors reproduced (88.4 percent): 28 of 32
transcript vectors (every SHAPE, DUPLICATE_ID, MODE and RETRY case, all 4 REPLAY cases and 7 of 8 UNKNOWN_REFERENCE
cases), 10 of 11 binding vectors. The five disagreements, each named and classed: B01, B02, B03 (the three valid
transcripts) and B17 (an UNKNOWN_REFERENCE case) all diverge at the same point: the lab's machine answers ACCEPTED where
the record answers CONCURRENCY_LIMIT. The lab read A2's "fewer than `concurrency` items held" as held by the
acquiring agent; A1 defines `concurrency` as "the most items held at once", board-wide, which the record applies.
One reading of one word; it accounts for 4 of the 5. R05 (binding, expected UNKNOWN_REFERENCE, the lab said BINDING)
turns on MAS-RA-002's record model refusing the manifest, which the lab's binding check validates by schema only: the
declared un-modelled dependency.

coordinator halves are now measured (52 of 52 and 38 of 43 from the records alone); the strategy half waits for its
record.
